newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Inmate dead as prisoners riot in Guatemala City.
newsitem.headline: Inmate dead as prisoners riot in Guatemala City.

text.p: A riot broke out in Guatemala City's main jail on Tuesday and one prisoner died after he was shot inside the compound, local radio reported.
Prisoners enraged by a security crackdown at the jail rioted for several hours, burning and destroying rooms before police and guards brought the uprising under control.
An army helicopter circled over the prison and police and guards inside and outside the compound fired warning shots into the air and launched tear gas at the rioters.

Radio Sonora said inmate Francis Mendez, 17, died in the San Juan de Dios Hospital from a bullet wound to the chest. No authorities were available to confirm the report and it was not clear how he was shot.
Javier Molina, spokesman for the Municipal Firemen, told reporters at least five other prisoners went to local hospitals suffering tear gas poisoning, bullet wounds and knife wounds.

During the riot, inmates took over a wing of the Zone 18 Prevention Centre, which holds 1,301 men mostly awaiting trial. The rioters threw rocks off the roof, burned mattresses, broke windows and destroyed rooms.

The prisoners were reacting to actions by jail administrators who, they said, curbed visiting rights and have cut meals since Sunday after the escape of a high-risk prisoner held on kidnapping charges.

"We are rioting because of the way they are treating us. They don't want to give us food and they want to take away visiting rights. We haven't eaten for three days and you know the people can't take it," an unidentified prisoner yelled to reporters near the entrance of the prison.

A large contingent of army and police reinforcements has surrounded the prison since the Sunday escape of Daniel Palacios, who government officials say is one of the leaders of a gang responsible for more than 20 kidnappings. Palacios was arrested in late January.
